title: Accordion
summary: Sections that open and close, built from data -- a record's groups, a settings panel, an FAQ, catalogue filters -- or from <details> in the markup, drawn as the class accordion: lines by default, the same sizes on the control ladder, appearances, marker and single section. The marker at the end points down and turns up when open, the section moves to its height in 200 ms; closed text is found by the browser's find-in-page; link makes a section's id its address; expand-all adds «Развернуть все». single keeps one open; the headers are buttons with the WAI-ARIA accordion keyboard.

template.description: Template variant name for SfBaseElement external templates.

root-class.description: Classes added to the root element the component draws.

root-style.description: Inline style declarations set on the root element the component draws, custom properties included.

single.description: One section open at a time: opening one closes the one that was open.

size.description: A step of the control ladder: the header is exactly the control height of the step, the height of an sf-input and an sf-button of the same size. Without it the roomy header of a content page.

appearance.description: flush, the default (owner decision C154 (2)): no fill and no radius, sections divided by a line -- quiet on a page, in a card and in a panel; default: filled plates a step apart; outline: a hairline border, no fill. An accordion inside a section draws lines whatever its appearance (C154 (8)).

marker.description: What marks a section open or closed: the chevron, or plus and minus.

single-section.description: One section is a plain section -- its content shown, its heading not a toggle; toggle keeps it a disclosure, for a list that fills in later.

heading-level.description: The level of each section's heading (role heading, aria-level).

link.description: A section's id is its address (owner decision C154 (5)): the section carries it as its element id, #id in the address opens the section and scrolls to it (on load and on hashchange), and opening a section by a press writes #id into the address with history.replaceState, without a new history entry.

expand-all.description: «Развернуть все / Свернуть все» (owner decision C154 (7)): a ghost button over the sections, at the end of the row, shown from five sections and never with single. It opens every section that can open; once all are open it reads «Свернуть все» and closes them. Each section that changes sends sf-accordion-toggle, source user.

items.description: The sections, [{id, title, content | slot, open?, disabled?, icon?, badge?, summary?}]: an array in the property, the same array as JSON in the attribute. Without items the element takes the <details> written inside it (data-id, data-icon, data-badge, data-summary, data-disabled).

id.description: The section's name in open(id), close(id), toggle(id) and the event; its place (section-1, section-2…) without it. One id names one section: a repeated one is left out.

content.description: The section's text. Text, never markup: markup goes in a slot.

slot.description: The name of a light-DOM slot holding the section's markup; it replaces content.

open.description: Open at first. In single mode only the first open section stays open.

disabled.description: Neither opened nor closed by the person: the header is a disabled button, out of the tab order.

icon.description: An icon before the title, a name from the icon font.

badge.description: A count or a label after the title, drawn by sf-badge.

summary.description: A short summary at the end of the header, before the marker, in the hint's colour (owner decision C154 (3)): «Выбрано 2», «Курьер». One line; a long one ends in an ellipsis.

id.description: The section's name in open(id), close(id), toggle(id) and the event; its place (section-1, section-2…) without it. One id names one section: a repeated one is left out.

content.description: The section's text. Text, never markup: markup goes in a slot.

slot.description: The name of a light-DOM slot holding the section's markup; it replaces content.

open.description: Open at first. In single mode only the first open section stays open.

disabled.description: Neither opened nor closed by the person: the header is a disabled button, out of the tab order.

badge.description: A count or a label after the title, drawn by sf-badge.

summary.description: A short summary at the end of the header, before the marker, in the hint's colour (owner decision C154 (3)): «Выбрано 2», «Курьер». One line; a long one ends in an ellipsis.

open.summary: Open the section with this id; in single mode the open one closes. sf-accordion-toggle fires for each section that changed, source method. Returns whether anything changed.

close.summary: Close the section with this id. Returns whether anything changed.

toggle.summary: Open the section if it is closed, close it if it is open. Returns whether anything changed.

isOpen.summary: Whether the section with this id is open. The single section always is.

sf-accordion:toggle.summary: A section opened or closed, by the person (source user) or by a method (source method). In single mode the section it closed sends its own, after the one asked for, as a native <details name> group does.

section.description: The section as the element draws it.

accessibility.focus: Each header is a native button inside a heading (role heading, aria-level), with aria-expanded and aria-controls; Enter and Space open and close it. ArrowDown and ArrowUp move between the headers and wrap, Home and End go to the first and the last; a disabled header is a disabled button, passed over and out of the tab order. Each panel is a region named by its header while there are six sections or fewer. The single section is a plain heading with nothing in the tab order.

ai_guidance.use_when: Use sf-accordion for sections that open and close and come from data -- a record's groups of fields, a settings panel, an FAQ, catalogue filters -- or are written as <details> in the markup. Nest at most one level (lines, under the outer title); deeper is sf-tree.
do_not: Do not copy generated ui-smart code
Do not put markup in content: it is shown as text; use a slot
Do not use it to switch between views of one thing: that is sf-tabs
Do not restyle its sections: they are the class accordion's, set its public variables
Do not nest accordions more than one level: deeper is a hierarchy, sf-tree
